title: Central covering of a reductive group by a torus and a simply connected semisimple group
statement:
Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure] and $G$ a reductive $F$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme]. Reductive means smooth, affine, of finite type and connected, with no nontrivial smooth connected normal unipotent subgroup; unipotent means that in a faithful matrix representation all geometric points are unipotent matrices. There exist an integer $r\geq0$, a semisimple simply connected $F$-group scheme $S$, and a faithfully flat homomorphism
$$p:T\times_F S\longrightarrow G,\qquad T=\mathbf G_{m,F}^{r},$$
with finite central kernel. Here $\mathbf G_m(A)=A^\times$ for every commutative $F$-algebra $A$. Semisimple means smooth, affine, connected and of finite type, with no nontrivial smooth connected solvable normal subgroup; solvable means that the successive commutator subgroup schemes eventually become trivial. Simply connected means that every surjective homomorphism $S'\to S$ with finite central kernel from a semisimple group scheme $S'$ is an isomorphism. A finite kernel has finite-dimensional coordinate algebra, and central means that it commutes with every element after every scalar extension. Faithful flatness means that $F[T\times S]$ is a faithfully flat $F[G]$-module: tensoring with it is exact and detects the zero module. In particular the pullback on coordinate algebras $p^*:F[G]\to F[T\times S]$ is injective. The cases $r=0$ and $S=1$ are allowed.

source.place: Proposition 21.60(a) implies (c), printed p.442; Proposition 19.21(c), pp.401--402; Theorem 18.25 and Remark 18.27, p.393; definition of central isogeny 18.1 and simply connected semisimple groups 19.15. Compose the almost-direct-product map with the simply connected covering of the derived subgroup.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-reductive-radical-quotient] to $G$ over $F$. It supplies a central torus $R=R(G)$ and a semisimple quotient $G/R$. Since $F$ is already algebraically closed, the torus clause gives an $F$-isomorphism $a:T=\mathbf G_m^r\xrightarrow{\sim}R$ for some $r\geq0$. All geometric hypotheses here are the given hypotheses over $F$.

Use [lem-sfb-central-torus-semisimple-derived-product] with this $R\subset G$: the quotient is semisimple by step 1. Obtain the semisimple group $D=G^{\mathrm{der}}$ and the multiplication map $m:R\times D\to G$, faithfully flat with finite central kernel of multiplicative type. Thus this map is a multiplicative isogeny; no assertion about its kernel is inferred merely from $F$-points.

Apply [lem-sfb-semisimple-multiplicative-universal-cover] to $D$. It gives a semisimple simply connected $S$ and $\pi:S\to D$ whose coordinate extension is faithfully flat and whose kernel $N$ is finite, central and of multiplicative type. This includes $D=1$.

For $H=D,S$, the product $T\times H$ is smooth over $F$: [lem-trf-split-lattice-torus-projection] with $L=\mathbf Z^r$ gives smoothness over $H$, and [lem-trf-smooth-composition] gives smoothness over $F$. The same torus node gives that $K[\mathbf Z^r]$ is a domain for every field extension $K/F$, so $T$ is geometrically connected. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-geometrically-connected-product-components] with $X=T$ and $Y=H$; since $H$ is connected, so is $T\times H$. Its coordinate ring is the tensor product of the two finitely generated coordinate rings, generated by their two finite sets of generators, so it is affine of finite type. Replace $T$ by $R$ via $a$ when needed.

Set $q=a\times\pi:T\times S\to R\times D$. This is a homomorphism, with kernel $1\times N$, hence finite and of multiplicative type. Write $B=F[D]$ and $C=F[S]$. For a module $M$ over $F[T]\otimes_F B$, tensor extension along $1\otimes\pi^*$ is canonically $M\otimes_B C$. Exactness and detection of zero follow from faithful flatness of $B\to C$; the isomorphism $a$ changes none of these properties. Thus $q$ is a multiplicative isogeny. The source and target have the required geometric properties by step 4.

source.place: Product construction 2.30; coordinate-ring tensor formula; definition of faithful flatness

proof.text: Define $p=m\circ q$, so $p(t,s)=a(t)\pi(s)$ in $G$. Apply [lem-sfb-multiplicative-isogeny-composition] to $q$ and $m$. Both are multiplicative isogenies of smooth connected affine finite-type groups by steps 2--5, so $p$ is faithfully flat with finite central scheme-theoretic kernel. This proves the required covering with the $r$ and $S$ already chosen.

Finally apply [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ideal-contraction] with $F[G]\to F[T\times S]$ and the zero ideal. It gives injectivity of $p^*$. The constructions allow $r=0$ or $S=1$; if $G=1$, both can be trivial.

proof_origin.place: Proposition 21.60(a)--(c), composed with Theorem 18.25/Remark 18.27 by Proposition 18.2; coordinate injectivity is Stacks Tag 05CK.

lean.statement: theorem reductive_torus_simplyConnected_cover {F : Type u} [Field F] [IsAlgClosed F] (G : Grp (Over (Spec (.of F)))) (hG : ReductiveTorusCentralizer.IsReductive G) : ∃ (r : ℕ) (S : Grp (Over (Spec (.of F)))), IsSemisimpleGroupScheme S.X ∧ (∀ (S' : Over (Spec (.of F))) [GrpObj S'], IsSemisimpleGroupScheme S' → ∀ (f : S' ⟶ S.X) [IsMonHom f], Surjective f.left → IsFinite (GrpObj.ker f).hom → (∀ (Z : Over (Spec (.of F))) (x : Z ⟶ GrpObj.ker f) (s : Z ⟶ S'), (x ≫ GrpObj.kerι f) * s = s * (x ≫ GrpObj.kerι f)) → IsIso f) ∧ ∃ (p : (MultiplicativeType.splitTorus F r).X ⊗ S.X ⟶ G.X) (_ : IsMonHom p), p.left.appTop.hom.FaithfullyFlat ∧ IsFinite (GrpObj.ker p).hom ∧ (∀ (Z : Over (Spec (.of F))) (x : Z ⟶ GrpObj.ker p) (g : Z ⟶ (MultiplicativeType.splitTorus F r).X ⊗ S.X), (x ≫ GrpObj.kerι p) * g = g * (x ≫ GrpObj.kerι p)) ∧ Function.Injective p.left.appTop.hom
